bulk.title: Import people from a spreadsheet
bulk.allOrNothing: All-or-nothing: if any row has a problem, nobody is imported.
bulk.instructions: Copy the rows from your spreadsheet — header row included — and paste them below. Columns can be in any order; only Name is required. Managers can be anyone in the same paste or already in the directory.

bulk.willAdd_other: {{count}} people will be added. Nothing has been written yet.

no_level.label: Not placed
no_level.description: Has no role, or a role with no level, so a report naming them cannot be escalated by rank. Give them a role, or give their role a level.

legacy_level.label: Old level, needs a role
legacy_level.description: Has no role; the level shown is left over from an old sync, so escalation can’t place them reliably. Give them a role.

manager_missing.label: Manager not on file
manager_missing.description: Their manager is not in the directory — usually someone who was removed — so they sit at the top of the chart.

manager_not_senior.label: Manager not more senior
manager_not_senior.description: Their manager sits at the same level or below them.

page.title: Reporting Hierarchy
page.seoDescription: Who a report escalates to: levels, the staff directory, and whether it all resolves.
page.intro: Who a report escalates to — someone above the person it names, never their peers or themselves.
page.viewOnlyBody: Your role can see the org chart — its levels and the people in it. Everything else here, and any change, is for admins.

leave.title: Leave without saving?
leave.message: Your changes to the escalation policy haven't been saved. They will be lost.

coverage.aliasAdded: "{{title}}" now maps to {{level}} from the next sync.
coverage.allPlaced: Everyone titled "{{title}}" already has a level.
coverage.addAliasHint: Future syncs suggest this level, and the role at it, for everyone with this title
coverage.giveRoleHint: Their role places them — and becomes the role on any account linked to them
coverage.resolvableBody: A report naming someone in the directory can be routed to the person above them.
coverage.resolvableGaps: Some gaps below may still leave individual reports for a human to route.
coverage.unresolvableBody: Every report will fall back to manual routing until the problems below are fixed.
coverage.unmappedBody: People with these titles can't be escalated from, and nobody can escalate to them.
coverage.noManagerBody: Escalation falls back to the nearest level above for these people, which is less precise than a real reporting line.
coverage.noGaps: No gaps found: every person has a level and a manager on file.

levelChart.lowestNeverTarget: Lowest level · never an escalation target
levelChart.peopleHint: People in the directory at this level
levelChart.loginHint: Directory entries with a login, and without one
levelChart.noAccounts: No accounts at this level yet.
levelChart.seeInDirectory: See the people at {{level}} in the directory
levelChart.unplacedBody: They have no role, or a role with no level. Escalation can't route a report around someone who isn't placed — give them a role, or give their role a level.
levelChart.unlinked_one: {{count}} account isn’t linked to the directory.
levelChart.unlinked_other: {{count}} accounts aren’t linked to the directory.
levelChart.unlinkedBody: They see only their own cases, whatever their role allows.
levelChart.noLevelsBody: The chart is drawn from your levels — the ladder a report escalates up. Add them first.
levelChart.clickRole: Click a role to see who holds it.

levelEditor.rankError: A whole number. Higher is more senior.
levelEditor.title: Title
levelEditor.codeHelpNew: Directory entries refer to the level by this. It cannot be changed later.
levelEditor.rankHelp: Higher is more senior. Leave gaps (10, 20, 30) so a level can be slotted in later.
levelEditor.departmentHelp: Restricts the level to one department. Empty means it applies everywhere.
levelEditor.aliasesTitle: Job titles from your HR system
levelEditor.aliasesHelp: The exact titles your HR system uses for people at this level — e.g. "Finance Manager" and "Sr. Finance Manager". During a sync, a matching title suggests this level, and the role that sits at it.
levelEditor.aliasesPlaceholder: Type a job title and press Enter
levelEditor.aliasesEmpty: No job titles yet. People are placed here by their role either way.
levelEditor.rolesHelp: A role's level is set on the role, and everyone holding it sits there. To put a role here, change its level in Roles & Permissions. Several roles can share a level.
levelEditor.notTargetHelp: Escalation passes through this level without stopping on it. For levels that oversee cases rather than handle them — an audit committee, external counsel. Leave it off otherwise; people who can't take a case are already skipped one by one. The lowest level is never a target either way.
levelEditor.activeHelp: An inactive level is ignored when resolving escalations.

levels.moveRolesFirst: Move these roles to another level first, then delete it.
levels.intro: Most senior first. A report escalates up this ladder.
levels.emptyBody: Start with the most senior tier and work down — e.g. Chief Executive, Director, Manager, Executive.
levels.deleteMessage: "{{title}}" will be removed from the ladder. A level can only be deleted once no role sits at it. To keep it for reference instead, edit it and turn off Active.

member.fromHrTitle: This person comes from your HR system
member.fromHrBody: A manager change is kept as a correction and survives the next sync. Other fields may be overwritten by it.
member.fullNameHelp: Spelled as a reporter would write it — escalation matches names in report text exactly.
member.employeeIdHelpNew: Optional — generated from the name if left empty.
member.sitsAt: Sits at {{level}}, with everyone else in this role.
member.roleNoLevel: This role has no level yet, so this person can't be placed until it gets one.
member.legacyLevel: Still on the old level ({{level}}). Give them a role to place them properly.
member.noRoleWarning: Without a role, a report naming this person can't be escalated.
member.moveHelp: To move someone, change their role. If the role itself is at the wrong level, change it in Roles & Permissions — that moves everyone who holds it.
member.accountSameRole: Their account, if they have one, gets the same role.
member.managerHelp: Escalation goes to the direct manager first, before the level ladder. A manager has to sit above this person.

picker.searchPlaceholder: Search name, email, title, employee id

directory.manualHint: Added by hand. Every sync leaves this entry alone.
directory.fromHrHint: Your HR system owns this entry. If a later HR pull no longer includes this person, they are deactivated automatically. (Someone added by hand who later appears in HR switches to this badge and keeps their corrections.)
directory.empty: No one in the directory yet
directory.noMatchBody: Try a different search or level.
directory.emptyBody: Add people by hand, paste a spreadsheet, or connect your HR system.
directory.noRoleHint: A person is placed by their role
directory.correctedHint: A person corrected the manager HR sent. The correction survives syncs.
directory.removeMessage: {{name}} was added by hand and will be removed from the directory permanently.
directory.deactivateMessage: {{name}} comes from your HR system, so they are deactivated rather than deleted — a real delete would be undone by the next sync. To remove them for good, remove them in HR.

node.legacyHint: Left over from an old sync — they have no role

routes.triage_queueHint: Held for a person to place by hand.

dest.triage: Triage, where a person places it

preview.typeOff: This report's type has escalation turned off, so it stays with the usual owner.
preview.oversightGap: Nobody with organization-wide access could open this case.
preview.needsReview: A name is uncertain. A handler must confirm who is meant.
preview.nothingChanged: Nothing was changed on the report.
preview.notFound: No report with that number in your organization.

warn.roleNotCleared: {{role}} can't open {{tier}} cases, which is the tier senior cases are raised to. Every senior case would end up in triage. Pick another role, or a lower tier.
warn.levelNoEscalations: {{level}} is set not to receive escalations, so senior cases would end up in triage.
warn.juniorLevel: This sends cases about senior people to a more junior level.

escalation.forbidden: You don't have permission to change the escalation policy.
escalation.emptyDirectory: Nobody is in the directory yet, so no report can be matched to a person.
escalation.intro: When a report is about someone in your directory, they never see it, and it goes to someone independent of them.

a.title: Finding who a report is about
a.detectLabel: Look for names in what reporters write
a.detectHelp: When a reporter writes the full name of someone in the directory, the report is treated as being about that person. When this is off, people are identified only when a reporter picks “My line manager” or a handler adds them.

b.title: Keeping them off the case
b.neverSees: The person a report is about never sees it: not in lists, search, exports or through a direct link, whatever their role.
b.ambiguous: If a name could belong to more than one person, all of them are kept off the case until a handler decides who is meant.
b.directReportsLabel: Also keep their direct reports off the case
b.directReportsHelp: Nobody should investigate their own manager. This only goes one level down. The person who filed the report is never kept off it.

c.title: Where the case goes
c.seniorFromHelp: People at this level or above are treated as senior. A report about them goes to the senior route below, not to their own manager.
c.raiseToHelp: A case about a senior person is raised to at least this confidentiality. It is never lowered.
c.levelHelp: Someone at this level who isn't kept off the case. If nobody is free, it goes to triage.
c.belowSenior: For anyone below the senior level, the case goes up their own reporting line to the nearest person who can take it. If nobody above them can, it goes to the report type's usual owner, and they are still kept off it.
c.perType: Each report type can also turn escalation off (in the report type builder, under Handling). Its reports still keep the person they're about off the case, but never go up the reporting line or to the senior route. If a type doesn't escalate, look there.

escalation.viewOnly: Changing the policy needs permission to manage the hierarchy.

d.title: {{letter}}. Try it on a report
d.description: Shows where a real report would go under the saved policy. Nothing on the report changes.
d.saveFirst: Save your changes to preview them.

bar.chooseRole: Choose a role for senior cases before saving.
bar.chooseLevel: Choose a level for senior cases before saving.
bar.unsaved: Unsaved changes to the escalation policy.

chart.dragHint: Drag the card onto someone to change their manager.

chart.gone: That person is no longer in the directory.
chart.cycle: {{target}} reports to {{member}}, so they can't be their manager.

chart.showing_one: Showing {{count}} person. Open a team with the count under a card.
chart.showing_other: Showing {{count}} people. Open a team with the count under a card.
chart.flagHint: {{description}} Counted among the people shown. Click to highlight them.

move.title: Change manager?

pending.intro: People your HR sync found for the first time. Give each a role — it also places them in the org chart — and decide whether they sign in, and how. Then approve. Answers save as you go and survive the next sync.

toast.allDirectory: Everyone waiting set to directory only.

bulk.methodLabel: Set a sign-in method for the selected people

empty.ready: Nobody is ready to approve yet
empty.dismissedBody: Dismissed people are skipped by every sync until you restage them.
empty.body: New people appear here after an HR sync finds them.

pending.footnote: Password accounts approved here start on the default password and must change it at first sign-in; Google and Microsoft accounts get no password. Bulk answers only touch people still waiting, never anyone already approved.

confirm.roleMessageLevel: All {{count}} people waiting will get the {{role}} role, which also places them in the org chart at {{level}}. Nobody is admitted yet.

confirm.directoryMessage: All {{count}} people waiting will be added without a login. Nobody is admitted yet.

sync.unreachable: Could not reach your HR system
sync.nothingChanged: Nothing in the directory was changed.

preview.noRecordsBody: Check the employees path, and the results path if the list is nested inside the response.
preview.skippedTitle_one: {{count}} record would be skipped for having no ID or name
preview.skippedTitle_other: {{count}} records would be skipped for having no ID or name
preview.skippedBody: This almost always means the mapping for Employee ID or Name points at the wrong field. A real sync drops these rows without saying so — fix the mapping and preview again before syncing.
preview.unmappedTitle: Job titles that match no level
preview.unmappedBody: People with these titles would sync with no level. Add each title to a level's job titles first, or map them on the Coverage tab after syncing.
preview.sampleNote: A sample of rows as they would be stored. Nothing has been written.

result.stagedNew: {{count}} found for the first time in this sync.
result.notAddedUntil: New people aren't added until you give them a level, decide whether they sign in, and approve them.
result.mapBody: People with these titles were synced with no level, so they can't be escalated from yet.
result.mapOnCoverage: Map them on the Coverage tab

toast.newWaiting_one: {{count}} new person is waiting for approval.
toast.newWaiting_other: {{count}} new people are waiting for approval.

sync.notConnectedBody: Connect any HR system that returns employees as JSON. Until then, add people by hand or paste them on the Directory tab.
sync.employeesPathHelp: The path (or full URL) that returns the list of employees.
sync.resultsPathHelp: Where the list sits inside the response, as a dot-path. Leave empty if the response is the list.
sync.headerApiKey: Often X-API-Key — check your HR system.

cred.savedHelp: A credential is saved and never shown again. Type a new one only to replace it.
cred.newHelp: Stored securely and never shown again.

graph.title: Microsoft Graph: check these before syncing
graph.resultsPath: Set Results path to value — Graph wraps the list in it.
graph.expand: Add $expand=manager($select=id) to the employees path and map manager.id, or nobody gets a manager and escalation can't route above anyone.
graph.paging: Only the first 100 people are read — later pages are ignored, and people missing from them are marked as having left. The token isn't refreshed either, so scheduled syncs stop working after about an hour.

sync.mappingHelp: The name of each field in your HR system's JSON. Use dots for nested fields — e.g. job.title.
sync.previewReadsOnly: Preview reads from your HR system and writes nothing.
sync.syncNowDirty: Save and preview your changes first
sync.syncNowHint: Pull from HR into the live directory
sync.previewAdvice: Preview before every first sync or mapping change — a wrong mapping otherwise looks like a successful sync of nobody.
sync.confirmMessage: This pulls every employee from your HR system into the live directory. People who were synced before but are missing from this pull will be deactivated. People added by hand, and corrections to level and manager, are kept.
